label: Junie CLI
description: One conversation with Junie CLI, JetBrains' coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Junie CLI runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `junie` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `junie` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, still on a local install, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. Its logins are offered on a local install only, since JetBrains' terms forbid providing Junie, or access to it, to anyone else, whatever login it runs on; so a cloud install has none to run it on. Before each turn Junie makes model calls of its own (a filter that picks which of your program's tools the turn gets, a task name, a title), which cost tokens on every message; a tool the filter left out the model can switch on itself. Commands it does not count as sensitive (`echo`) run without asking in every setting. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, the effort and instructions added to its guidelines. Your program's tools reach Junie's model as tools of its `weft` MCP server, and come back to your program under their plain names. Junie cannot let a program's tool take one of its own tools' places, so a tool named like one of them (`bash`, `search_project`, `search_replace` and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Junie CLI in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A JunieCliAccess's `access`: a Junie token or a model provider's key (on a local install). Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Junie uses the login already on it: run `junie` once and log in with your JetBrains account (it keeps the login in `~/.junie`, or in the system keyring where there is one), or wire one here with a token from https://junie.jetbrains.com/cli.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Junie CLI works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Junie CLI program to run, when it is not the `junie` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Junie CLI may do without asking. `ask`: every action it counts as sensitive comes out of AskAgent as a question. `auto`: its own safety check lets the commands it judges safe through and asks about the rest. `plan`: a planning agent with read-only tools. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: A model the login offers (`gemini-3.6-flash`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gpt-5.5`, ...): `junie list-models` lists more than a login may run, and one the login does not offer is refused as the conversation starts, naming those it does. Left out, Junie's default, or the LiteLLM proxy's own model.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How much the model reasons; each model takes some of these. Left out, the model's default.

inputs.name: appendSystemPrompt
inputs.label: Add to its guidelines
inputs.description: Instructions added to the agent's guidelines, for the whole conversation.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: JunieCli '{id}' runs on a local install only: JetBrains' terms forbid providing Junie, or access to it, to anyone else, so a cloud install offers it no login, with or without a Computer.
JunieCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a JunieCliAccess on `access`.
JunieCli '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
JunieCli '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, auto, plan, bypass.
JunieCli '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
JunieCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Junie CLI itself.
